# Daily #progress update

Builds the daily update for `#progress` (`C09MB3TPBFF`, entireio.slack.com) from evidence,
in Andrea's voice, and stops for review.

**Hard rule: never post.** Never call `slack_send_message` or `slack_schedule_message` for
this channel. The only write allowed is `slack_send_message_draft`, and only after the user
has seen the text and said yes. A draft lands in Slack's *Drafts & Sent* where they edit and
send it themselves.

## 1. Pick the window

Find the last update Andrea posted in the channel:

```
slack_search_public_and_private(
  query="from:<@U0AJ0FHDXFW> in:<#C09MB3TPBFF>",
  sort="timestamp", limit=5, include_context=false)
```

Ignore short replies and thread messages, look for the last real bulleted update. The window
runs from that message to now. If there's a multi-day gap (weekend, OOO), cover the gap and
lead with `- Catch-up`, which is what he does.

Times are Europe/Rome. Get "now" from the shell (`date`), never assume.

## 2. Gather evidence

Run these together, they're independent.

**Trails** (the primary source, most bullets link one). Repos live in `/Users/nodo/work/entire/*`.
For each repo with a `.git`:

```bash
entire trail list --author me --status any --json -n 20
```

Keep trails whose `created_at`/`updated_at`/`merged_at` fall in the window. Useful fields:
`url`, `title`, `status` (draft/open/merged/closed), `phase`, `branch`.

**Commits**, which catch work with no trail and unpushed work:

```bash
git -C <repo> log --all --author="andrea@entire.io" --since="<window start>" --format="%h %s"
```

`--all` matters: trail work sits on branches, so plain `git log` (HEAD only) misses it.

**Cross-repo backstop**, covering repos not cloned locally and pushes from elsewhere:
`get_entire_my_activity(scope="commits", since=..., until=...)` on `entire-prod-us`.
This returns full commit bodies and is very verbose. Read `repo_full_name` and
`commit_subject`, skip the rest. `commit_message` is null for native repos, local git
fills those in.

**Linear**, which gives each item its ticket ID and title:

```
list_issues(assignee="me", updatedAt="-P1D", limit=20,
            fields=["title","url","status","updatedAt","team"])
```
(`-P3D` or wider for a catch-up. Note: `identifier` is not a valid field, the ID comes back
as `id`.)

**Incidents / firefighting**: `incident_list(assigned_to=["me"], created_after=..., include=["summary"])`.
Also worth a look: alerts he chased in `#alerts-production` (`C0B1Y3Y6PFD`).

**His own words elsewhere.** He often links a thread he wrote in another channel rather than
re-explaining:

```
slack_search_public_and_private(
  query="from:<@U0AJ0FHDXFW> after:<window start> -in:<#C09MB3TPBFF>",
  sort="timestamp", include_context=false)
```

Grab permalinks for substantial design or decision messages. Skip chit-chat.

## 3. Write it

Read `style.md` in this skill directory before writing. It has the rules and real examples.
Two rules matter most: **no em dashes**, and **be concise**.

Group the evidence into 2 to 6 themes, not a flat dump of every commit. Twelve commits
refactoring one thing is one bullet with the theme as the headline. Judge by what a reader
cares about, not by diff size.

State what changed and why it mattered, not what you touched. "Fixed a tricky bug when a github
mirror changes ownership" beats "updated mirror teardown logic".

Every claim needs evidence from step 2 behind it. Don't infer that something shipped because a
trail exists, check `status`. Don't invent ticket IDs. If a trail is still `open`, say in
progress or put it under **In progress**. Leave out anything you can only guess at. A shorter
honest update is the right outcome on a quiet day.

## 4. Review, then draft

Save it to `/Users/nodo/work/entire/progress/<YYYY-MM-DD>.md`, one file per update. That also
builds a local archive of past posts to check tone against.

Show the full text in the terminal and ask whether to create the Slack draft. Offer that it's
easy to adjust: wrong emphasis, a missing meeting, something that shouldn't be public.

Only when they approve:

```
slack_send_message_draft(channel_id="C09MB3TPBFF", message="<text>")
```

Then tell them it's waiting in *Drafts & Sent* in `#progress`, unsent.

If it returns `draft_already_exists`, say so. Slack allows one draft per channel, so they need
to send or delete the existing one first. Don't work around it by posting.

## Notes

- Slack user ID: `U0AJ0FHDXFW`. Channel: `C09MB3TPBFF`.
- Meetings, reviews, design discussions and OOO notices count as progress. Engineering output
  is most of it, but a day of unblocking others is worth saying.
- If the day genuinely produced little, a one-liner is fine and in character
  (`- Working on making NATS more robust :thinkies:`).

# Andrea's #progress voice

Distilled from two months of his posts. Match this, don't improve on it.

## Hard rules

**No em dashes.** Never use `—` or `–`. Use a comma, a colon, parentheses, or split the
sentence. This applies to the draft and to anything you say about it.

**Be concise.** One line per item. If a bullet runs past two lines, cut it or move the detail
into a sub-bullet. A reader should get the day in fifteen seconds.

- Cut throat-clearing: "I spent time on", "worked on", "made progress with", "continued to".
  Say what changed.
- Cut hedges and intensifiers: "quite", "fairly", "significantly", "really".
- One fact per bullet. Two facts means two bullets, or one bullet and a sub-bullet.
- Don't explain the mechanism unless the mechanism is the point. Numbers beat adjectives:
  `halved the p50 / p95 duration of mirror worker`.

## Shape

- Bullets, no prose paragraphs. Top level `- `, nested one level with 4-space indent.
  (Slack renders these as `•` and `◦`.)
- No greeting, no sign-off, no closing summary.
- One line to ~20. Length follows the day, not a template.
- Optional one-line opener when the day had a shape worth naming, then a blank line:
  `Busy day :whack-a-mole:` / `A bit all over the place today:` / `:bug: bashing:`
- Optional plain-text group headers ending in a colon: `Mirror pipeline reliability:`,
  `Done:` / `In progress:` / `Next:`. Use them for 3+ themes, skip them on a short day.
- Emoji as theme markers, leading a bullet or standing as a section head. His set:
  `:bug:` `:fire:` `:firefighter:` `:pager:` `:nats:` `:mirror:` `:kubernetes:` `:rocket:`
  `:broom:` `:merged:` `:pr-open:` `:white_check_mark:` `:test_tube:` `:thinkies:` `:bulb:`
  `:yak:` `:palm_tree:` `:whack-a-mole:`
  Sparingly, and only where they carry meaning. Half his posts have none.

## Voice

- First person, terse, lowercase-leaning. "we" for things the team shipped together.
- Says what changed and why it mattered, in one clause. No adjectives selling the work.
  - ✅ `Fixed a race condition while executing mirrors teardown`
  - ❌ `Made significant improvements to the robustness of the teardown flow`
- Honest about mess: "this was a really subtle bug", "this keeps biting us", "still in progress",
  "I decided against a reconciler".
- Occasional aside for the team: `:bulb: ICYMI I did a big refactoring of the fanout services`,
  or `tl;dr` before a compressed explanation.
- `cc @person` when someone owns the area or should review.

## Links

Nearly every substantive bullet carries one.

- Linear: label is the bare ticket ID, `[COR-1223](url)`, then ` - ` and the description.
- Trails: `[entire.io/gh/entirehq/…/2088](url)` or a descriptive title as the label.
- GitHub PRs where the repo isn't on Entire.
- Slack permalinks to a thread in another channel, instead of re-explaining it.
- Channel refs for incidents: `<#C0BBHD98XQE|incident-2026-06-18-mirror-pipeline-401s>`.

Short day:

```
- Working on making NATS more robust :thinkies:
```

Ordinary day:

```
- Fixed the repo ops nats config, added a DLQ and made sure we don't leave jobs behind after max redelivery is exhausted
- Fixed a bug with teardown / tidied up observability
- Long investigation for the core latency issues on mirror create ([COR-947](url))
- Created a small tool to visualize our NATS streams consumer and producers [artifact](url)
```

Themed, with sub-bullets:

```
- Perms-sweep: fixed the EpicGames/UnrealEngine fork-network blowup. Large fork networks made the sweep fetch enormous per-fork collaborator lists, surfacing the reconcile/mint-token failures the perms-sweep monitors fire on.
    - Banned that specific repo and its fork
    - Re-run backfilling of all the repos we have access to, run successfully without issues cc @James @Alex
- Fixed cross-region mirror-create false failures. Added 20s mutation timeout + idempotent write-retry.
- Ingest: don't skip fresh-repo history import on a multi-branch first sync. This was a really subtle bug ([ENT-1167](url) for more details). fyi @vydra as you worked on this area.
```

```

Text: 
```Stripped down: the indexer treats "not ready yet" as "failed."

That one category error produces everything else:

- Wrong budget. Hydration lag gets a retry envelope sized for transient errors — ~42–45 min, now a hard invariant. Nothing bounds how long hydration actually takes, so the budget is unrelated to the thing it's supposedly waiting for.
- Wrong granularity. The verdict is per-event, so 2 unready checkpoints out of 11 throw away the 9 healthy ones' completed work — five times over, then permanently.
- Wrong finality. On give-up the event dead-letters, and because ref events are keyed on old_target→new_target transitions, the next event starts past the dropped range. Nothing revisits it. A "wait a bit longer" condition ends as a permanent hole in the search index.```

That one category error produces everything else:

- Wrong budget. Hydration lag gets a retry envelope sized for transient errors — ~42–45 min, now a hard invariant. Nothing bounds how long hydration actually takes, so the budget is unrelated to the thing it's supposedly waiting for.
- Wrong granularity. The verdict is per-event, so 2 unready checkpoints out of 11 throw away the 9 healthy ones' completed work — five times over, then permanently.
- Wrong finality. On give-up the event dead-letters, and because ref events are keyed on old_target→new_target transitions, the next event starts past the dropped range. Nothing revisits it. A "wait a bit longer" condition ends as a permanent hole in the search index.```
